chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Washshāʾ, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding two men who had stolen from the property of Allah. One of them was a slave, the property of Allah, and the other was from the property of the people. So he said: “As for this one, he is from the property of Allah; there is nothing upon him. The property of Allah has consumed some of it by another part. But as for the other, he brought him forward and cut off his hand.”
Then he ordered that he be fed ghee and meat until his hand healed.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in the report
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment; issued a legal ruling
key_terms.قَطَعَ يَدَهُ: cut off his hand; applied the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.مَالِ اللَّهِ: the property of Allah, meaning property held in the public domain

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام judge between two theft cases involving public property and the property of the people?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning theft, distinguishing between a slave who was considered from the public property and another person who stole from the people's property. It highlights the application of the hadd in theft cases and also records the instruction to care for the punished person until he recovered.
